input.reasoning: Backlog of 24 items spans auth/security, payments, data migration, UX, and infra work across 4 roles with limited capacity (1.5 Backend FTE, 1.0 Frontend FTE, 0.6 QA FTE, 0.4 DevOps FTE — total ~3.5 FTE). I estimated effort per task using story points where given (roughly 1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted per task complexity and role mix) and analogous sizing for unestimated tasks based on description complexity, comparing to similarly-scoped estimated tasks. I then split each task's hours across roles based on the nature of the work (e.g., backend-heavy for RBAC/payments/migration, frontend-heavy for dashboards/UI work, QA and DevOps for verification/infra), and finally aggregated all tasks into role totals. Given the constrained capacity (esp. DevOps at 0.4 FTE and QA at 0.6 FTE), I flagged that these roles are thinly staffed relative to backlog scope, likely stretching timeline. I built three delivery scenarios (P50 base, P80 realistic-with-risk, P90 conservative-with-contingency) reflecting integration risk (Stripe, legacy Oracle migration), unestimated tasks' inherent uncertainty, and no historical actuals to calibrate against. Non-labour costs include Stripe sandbox/production fees, staging infra, and a data-migration tooling/environment allowance. Reductions target descoping/deferring Low-priority items (support ticket sync, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, legacy decommission) and trimming accessibility/multi-currency scope, plus deferring non-critical DevOps observability work.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base estimate (planned scope, normal execution)
P90 - Conservative with contingency for unestimated items and thin staffing

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees, sandbox/testing and PCI-related tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling and temporary environment (ETL/validation)
Observability/tracing platform licensing (e.g. Datadog/New Relic) setup
Contingency buffer for unestimated tasks (10% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is based purely on story points, task descriptions, and analogous sizing.

1 story point is treated as roughly 6-7 hours of blended cross-role effort for estimated tasks; unestimated tasks were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped estimated tasks (e.g. PW-2 component library sized similarly to PW-5/PW-13; PW-8 legacy migration sized larger than any single estimated task due to data volume and risk).

Role capacity is tightly constrained: DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) and QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the backlog's infra and testing needs; hours allocated reflect proportionate stretch across the project timeline rather than full parallel capacity, which will lengthen calendar duration or require reprioritization.
Backend Developer carries the largest share of hours due to payment integration, RBAC, migration, 2FA, rate limiting, and audit log work, consistent with 1.5 FTE capacity.
Frontend Developer hours cover dashboard, invoice UI, design system, accessibility, responsive layout and admin back-office work.
QA Engineer hours are concentrated on high-risk areas (payments, auth, migration, GDPR) rather than full regression coverage of every task, given limited capacity.
DevOps Engineer hours are concentrated on CI/staging setup (PW-1), observability (PW-22), and migration/infra support, with limited time for anything beyond critical-path infra work.
Non-labour costs assume mid-tier SaaS/cloud pricing for a project of this size over an assumed ~6-9 month delivery window.
Priority breakdown totals are labour-only estimates allocated by matching each task's priority label to its estimated hour allocation across roles.
Scenario spread (P50/P80/P90) reflects integration risk on Stripe webhooks/reconciliation, legacy Oracle migration complexity, and general uncertainty in unestimated backlog items.

reductions.description: Descope or defer Low-priority items (PW-12 support ticket submission, PW-18 admin back-office, PW-19 usage analytics, PW-23 contract tests, PW-24 legacy decommission) to a later phase
reductions.effect: Removes ~5 low-priority backlog items from initial delivery scope, reducing Frontend/Backend/QA hours across the board

reductions.description: Reduce Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope to critical customer-facing screens only rather than full WCAG 2.2 AA across all screens in this phase
reductions.effect: Cuts ~90 Frontend Developer + QA hours by narrowing initial accessibility scope

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14) to a post-launch release since only USD is required for initial go-live
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated ~150 Backend/Frontend hours from current phase

reductions.description: Simplify Legacy data migration (PW-8) by migrating in phased batches (active accounts first) instead of full 400k/2M record migration up front
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer and DevOps migration/validation hours in this phase by roughly 200 hours

reductions.description: Defer Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) beyond payment-path alerting to a follow-up sprint
reductions.effect: Reduces DevOps Engineer hours and observability licensing cost
